title: 4GE1-style exam questions: coastal environments (Paper 1, Topic 2)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 24 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 24: Revision: coastal environments (Paper 1, Topic 2). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Timed answer (10 minutes): 'Evaluate the effectiveness of coastal management in a developed and a developing or emerging country.' Portal response box.
questions.a: Two named places; strategies and outcomes; strengths and weaknesses with evidence; comparison; substantiated judgement
questions.model: Teacher plans: P1 developed example: strategy, success, problem; P2 developing or emerging example; P3 comparison (cost, technology, sustainability); conclusion.

questions.a: A precise target linked to the mark points

questions.q: Suggest why soft engineering is often more sustainable.
questions.a: Works with natural processes (1), lower cost and maintenance (1), less impact on other parts of the coast (1)

questions.q: Explain the formation of a stack.
questions.a: Crack in headland widened by hydraulic action and abrasion (1); cave forms (1); erosion through the headland forms an arch (1); roof collapses leaving a stack (1)
questions.model: Sequence: crack, cave, arch, stack. At each stage name the process: hydraulic action, abrasion. Finish with the roof collapsing through weathering and erosion.

questions.q: State two threats to coral reefs.
questions.a: Two of: ocean warming (bleaching), pollution, overfishing, tourism damage
Allowing the coast to erode or flood in a controlled way

questions.q: Big question: should every coastline be defended?
questions.a: No: cost, effects downdrift and sustainability mean some areas are best left to managed retreat, while high-value places are protected
